academic_translation: In the language of India: Bodhisattvacaryāvatāra.
translation: In the language of India: Bodhisattvacharyavatara.

academic_translation: In the language of Tibet: Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva.

locked_terms.use: Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero

translation: In the language of Tibet: Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero.

academic_translation: Homage to all Buddhas and bodhisattvas.
translation: I bow down to all the Buddhas and awakening heroes.

academic_translation:
To the Sugatas who possess the Dharmakāya, along with their sons,
And to all who are worthy of homage, I respectfully bow down;
The engagement in the vows of the sons of the Sugata
I shall state concisely, in accordance with scripture.
translation: I bow down with respect to the Well-Gone Ones who have the truth body, and to their children. I also bow to everyone who deserves respect. I will briefly explain how to keep the promises of the children of the Well-Gone One. I will explain this by following the sacred texts.
I am not saying anything new here. I am also not very good at writing. Because of this, I did not write this to help others. I wrote this just to train my own mind.

academic_translation:
In order to cultivate virtue, the force of my faith
Will, for a time, increase through these;
And if others, equal in fortune to myself,
Should see these, they will become meaningful.
translation: To practice good deeds, the power of my faith will grow for a while through these words. If other people who are as lucky as me see them, these words will become meaningful.

academic_translation:
This leisure and endowment is extremely difficult to find;
Since that which accomplishes human purpose has been attained,
If one does not accomplish what is beneficial with this,
How will this be perfectly found again later?
translation: This free and fortunate life is very hard to find. We have gained what we need to reach the purpose of a human life. If we do not use this life to do what is helpful, how will we ever find it perfectly again?

academic_translation:
Just as on a dark night, within a dense mass of clouds,
A flash of lightning shows brilliant illumination for an instant,
Likewise, by the power of the Buddha, once in a hundred times,
Intelligence for merit rarely arises in the world.
translation: On a dark night covered in thick clouds, a flash of lightning makes everything bright for a second. In the same way, by the power of the Buddha, the mind to build a store of goodness rarely appears in the world. It only happens once in a hundred times.

academic_translation:
Therefore, virtue is always feeble,
While misdeeds are extremely powerful and unbearable;
Except for the bodhicitta for perfect awakening,
What other virtue could overcome them?
translation: Because of this, a good deed is always weak. But harmful deeds are very strong and hard to bear. Besides the awakening mind for full awakening, what other good deed could ever defeat them?

academic_translation:
The Lords of Sages, having thoroughly contemplated for many eons,
Have seen that this alone is beneficial.
By this, limitless multitudes of beings
Will easily attain supreme happiness.
translation: The Lords of Sages thought deeply for many great ages. They saw that only this is helpful. With it, countless beings will easily find the greatest happiness.

academic_translation:
Those who wish to overcome the hundreds of sufferings of existence,
Who wish to dispel the unhappiness of sentient beings,
And who wish to enjoy many hundreds of joys,
Should never forsake bodhicitta.
translation: Some people want to end the hundreds of sufferings of life. Some want to take away the sadness of living beings. Others want to enjoy hundreds of joys. All of them should never give up the awakening mind.

academic_translation:
When bodhicitta is generated, in an instant,
The wretched bound in the prison of saṃsāra
Will be called the children of the Sugatas,
And will be paid homage by the world, including its gods and humans.
translation: As soon as the awakening mind is born, everything changes in a flash. Poor beings trapped in the prison of the cycle of rebirth will be called children of the Well-Gone Ones. The whole world, including gods and humans, will bow down to them.

academic_translation:
Like the supreme form of a gold-making elixir,
It takes this impure body and transforms it
Into the priceless jewel of a Victor's body;
Therefore, firmly hold to what is called bodhicitta.
translation: It is like the very best gold-making potion. It takes this impure body and turns it into the priceless jewel of a Victorious One's body. Therefore, hold tightly to the awakening mind.

academic_translation:
Since the sole caravan leader of wandering beings, with limitless intellect,
Has thoroughly examined it and found it to be highly precious,
Those who wish to be separated from the realms of wandering beings
Should firmly hold to precious bodhicitta.
translation: The one leader of travelers for all beings has a limitless mind. He looked at it closely and saw how precious it is. Anyone who wants to leave the homes of beings should hold tightly to the precious awakening mind.

academic_translation:
All other virtues are like the plantain tree:
Having produced a result, they are exhausted;
But the tree of bodhicitta perpetually
Yields a result, is not exhausted, and increases.
translation: All other good deeds are like a banana tree. After giving a result, they are used up. But the tree of the awakening mind always gives a result. It never runs out, and it keeps growing.

academic_translation:
Even if one has committed extremely unbearable misdeeds,
Just as relying on a hero frees one from great fear,
By relying on which one will be freed in an instant,
Why do the conscientious not rely on it?
translation: Even if you have done a terrible harmful deed, this mind will free you in an instant. It is like relying on a brave hero to escape great fear. Why wouldn't careful people rely on it?

academic_translation:
Like the fire at the end of time, it
Certainly burns up great misdeeds in a single instant.
Its immeasurable benefits
Were explained to Sudhana by the wise Protector Maitreya.
translation: It is like the fire at the end of time. It completely burns up great mistakes in a single instant. The wise Protector Maitreya explained its endless benefits to Sudhana.

academic_translation:
In brief, that bodhicitta
Should be understood to be of two types:
Aspiring bodhicitta and
Engaging bodhicitta itself.

locked_terms.use: mind that sets out to awaken

translation: In short, you should know that the awakening mind has two types. They are the mind that wishes to awaken and the mind that sets out to awaken.

academic_translation:
Between wishing to go and going,
Just as one understands the difference,
Likewise, a wise person should understand
The difference between these two in their respective order.
translation: Think about the difference between wanting to go somewhere and actually going. A wise person should understand the difference between these two minds in the exact same way.

academic_translation:
From aspiring bodhicitta,
Although a great result arises while in saṃsāra,
Unlike from engaging bodhicitta,
Merit does not arise continuously.

locked_terms.use: mind that sets out to awaken

translation: The mind that wishes to awaken brings a great result in the cycle of rebirth. But a store of goodness does not grow from it continuously. That only happens with the mind that sets out to awaken.

academic_translation:
From the moment that, to thoroughly liberate
The infinite realm of sentient beings,
With an irreversible mind,
One correctly adopts that mind,
translation: You might truly take up this mind to completely free the endless realm of living beings. You make this choice with a mind of never turning back. From that very moment...

academic_translation:
From this moment onward, whether asleep,
Or falling into heedlessness, a force of merit,
Uninterrupted and manifold,
Continually arises, equal to space.
translation: From this moment on, a huge store of goodness keeps growing. It happens even if I am asleep or acting with carelessness. It never stops, and it is as big as space.

academic_translation:
Together with the reasoning for this,
In the Question of Subāhu,
For the sake of sentient beings with lesser inclinations,
The Tathāgata himself proclaimed this.
translation: The Thus-Gone One himself explained this. He gave the reasons for it in the teaching called the Question of Subahu. He said this to help living beings who are just starting out.

academic_translation:
If even by thinking, "I shall dispel
The mere headaches of sentient beings,"
One possesses a beneficial intention
And becomes endowed with immeasurable merit,
translation: If someone just thinks, 'I will cure the headaches of every living being,' they have a kind wish. They gain an immeasurable store of goodness.

academic_translation:
Wishing to dispel the immeasurable discomforts
Of each and every sentient being,
And wishing to accomplish immeasurable good qualities
For each one—what need is there to mention this?
translation: What if someone wants to take away the immeasurable pain of every living being? What if they want to build up immeasurable good qualities for each one? We do not even need to ask how great that is!

academic_translation:
Whether it be a father or even a mother,
Who has such a beneficial intention?
Whether gods or seers,
Does even Brahmā have this?
translation: Who else has such a kind wish? Does a father or even a mother have it? Do the gods or a wise seer? Does even Brahma have this wish?

academic_translation:
If, for those very sentient beings previously,
Such a mind for their own sake
Was never dreamed of even in a dream,
How could it arise for the sake of others?
translation: Before now, those living beings never dreamed of this kind of wish for themselves. So how could they ever have it for anyone else?

academic_translation:
That intention for the welfare of sentient beings,
Which does not arise in others even for their own sake—
This extraordinary jewel of a mind
Is born as an unprecedented wonder.
translation: Most people do not have this wish even for themselves. But this wish to help every living being is born as a brand new wonder. It is an amazing jewel of a mind.

academic_translation:
The cause of joy for all wandering beings,
The medicine for the suffering of sentient beings—
The merit of such a precious mind,
How could it ever be measured?
translation: This mind brings joy to all beings. It is the medicine for the suffering of living beings. How could anyone ever measure the store of goodness of such a precious mind?

academic_translation:
If even the mere intention to be beneficial
Is more exalted than making offerings to the Buddhas,
Then for all sentient beings without exception,
What need is there to mention striving for their happiness?
translation: Just wishing to help is better than making offerings to the Buddhas. So, what need is there to mention working hard for the happiness of every single living being?

academic_translation:
Although they have the wish to discard suffering,
They rush headlong into suffering itself;
Although they desire happiness, through ignorance
They destroy their own happiness as if it were an enemy.
translation: People want to throw away their suffering, but they run right into it. They want happiness. But because of ignorance, they destroy their own happiness as if it were an enemy.

academic_translation:
For those who are destitute of happiness
And who have many sufferings,
That which satisfies them with all happiness
And cuts through all suffering,
translation: Some people have no happiness and face so much suffering. This mind fills them with happiness and cuts through all their suffering.

academic_translation:
And it even dispels their ignorance.
Where is there a virtue equal to that?
Where is there a friend like that?
Where is there even merit like that?
translation: It even clears away their ignorance. Where is there a good deed equal to that? Where is there a friend like that? Where is there a store of goodness like that?

academic_translation:
If whoever repays a benefit done to them
Is indeed worthy of some praise,
What need is there to mention the bodhisattva
Who does good without being asked?
translation: People praise someone who pays back a favor. So we should definitely praise the awakening hero who does good things without even being asked.

academic_translation:
One who provides regular food to a few wandering beings,
Giving merely a meal for a brief moment,
And satisfying them for half a day with contempt,
Is honored by people as a doer of virtue.
translation: Think about someone who feeds a few beings. They might just give one quick meal. They might even be mean while feeding them. Still, people honor them for doing a good deed.

academic_translation:
To limitless numbers of sentient beings for a long time,
The unsurpassed happiness of the Sugatas,
Given constantly so as to fulfill all the wishes in their minds—
What need is there to mention one who gives thus?
translation: Now think of someone who gives the greatest happiness of the Well-Gone Ones to countless living beings for a long time. They give constantly to make every wish come true. Imagine how wonderful that person is!

academic_translation:
If anyone toward such a benefactor, a child of the Victors,
Generates a malicious thought, that one,
For eons equal to the number of malicious thoughts generated,
Will abide in hell, so the Sage has taught.
translation: What if someone thinks bad thoughts about such a kind child of the Victorious Ones? The Sage taught that for every bad thought, they will stay in hell for a great age.

academic_translation:
But if anyone develops a deeply devoted mind,
Its result increases even more than that.
Even in great adversity for the children of the Victors,
Misdeeds do not arise, and virtue naturally increases.
translation: But if someone feels deep respect for them, the result is even greater. Even in hard times, a child of the Victorious Ones does no harmful deeds. Their good deeds just naturally grow.

academic_translation:
In whomever that supreme, precious mind
Has arisen, I bow to their body;
And those to whom even doing harm connects one to happiness—
I go for refuge to those sources of happiness.
translation: I bow down to anyone who has grown this perfect, precious mind. Even if someone hurts them, they still connect that person to happiness. I go for shelter to these sources of happiness.

academic_translation: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, this is the first chapter, called Explaining the Benefits of Bodhicitta.

locked_terms.use: Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero

translation: This is the first chapter from Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero. It is called Explaining the Benefits of the Awakening Mind.
